Preview the pseudobulk profiles of an object

pseudobulk_design.Rd

Metadata-only companion of pseudobulk(): resolves the same sample x group profiles (same rows, same order) and reports how many cells each one has, without reading any expression data. Use it to check replication before aggregating, e.g. whether every group has enough samples, or whether samples contribute cells to several groups (a paired design).

Usage

pseudobulk_design(object, sample_by, group_by = NULL, cells = NULL)

Arguments

object

A single cell object. Currently, Seurat, SingleCellExperiment, and anndata objects are supported.

sample_by

The sample (biological replicate) of each cell: the name of a metadata column, or a character/factor vector named by cell (one label per cell of the object, or at least per cell in cells). A vector lets a caller aggregate by labels that are not stored in the object.

group_by

Optional group of each cell (same forms as sample_by). With NULL the profiles are the samples themselves.

cells

A character vector of cell names to include, as they are named in the object (i.e. according to colnames(object)). If NULL, data will be returned for all cells in the object.

Value

An object of class scuba_pseudobulk_design: a list with profiles (as in pseudobulk()), table (samples x groups matrix of cell counts; one column when group_by is NULL), paired (TRUE when any sample has cells in more than one group), samples_per_group (samples with at least one cell per group), samples_in_all_groups, n_cells_dropped, n_cells (cells assigned to a profile), sample_by and group_by.

Examples

d <- pseudobulk_design(AML_Seurat, "Batch", "condensed_cell_type")
d$table
#>            B Cells BM Monocytes CD4+ T Cells CD8+ T Cells Dendritic cells
#> BM_200AB        14           25            8           17              15
#> PBMC_200AB      11            0           17            8              10
#>            NK Cells Plasma cells Plasmacytoid dendritic cells Primitive
#> BM_200AB         18           12                           19        24
#> PBMC_200AB        7           13                            6         1
#>            PBMC Monocytes
#> BM_200AB                0
#> PBMC_200AB             25
d$paired
#> [1] TRUE
